newsitem.title: GERMANY: German new crop wheat sellers aim for higher price.
newsitem.headline: German new crop wheat sellers aim for higher price.

text.p: Nominal German new crop wheat prices have gained up to 10 marks on the week but there is no fresh business to report, brokers said.
"It's the typical stand-off between buyers and sellers ahead of the harvest," one said.
"Sellers argue French qualities are not great but buyers say German and British qualities will be fine and they can afford to wait."
Barley harvesting was nearly complete in northern German export regions while wheat harvesting will start at the end of this week at the earliest.
Farmers were busy harvesting rapeseed and not concerned with grain marketing.
Because of frequent rainfall in July, they were aiming to bring in the harvest as quickly as possible to avoid drying costs and damage.
Barley prices ex-harvest were rising because much spot barley had already been placed with buyers at country merchant and co-op level.
The bulk of supply was being stored away to bring higher prices in the autumn.

Northern German barley harvests were between 75 and 90 percent complete, moisture at 15 to 18 percent and yields of 6.00 to 10.00 tonnes per hectare -- above Germany's national average yield of 5.61 tph last year.
The Hamburg grain exchange left its spot bread wheat price (220 hagberg, 12.5 percent protein) at 267.50 marks/tonne without quoting a spot feed wheat price.
Spot feed wheat last week was 262.50 marks and the latest September feed wheat price was at 265 marks.
German fob levels for new crop wheat were starting at 275 for 12 percent Aug/Sept wheat in the 3,000 lot size.
A wide range of qualities, shipment sizes and dates up to December were available, with top prices for 10,000 tonnes Sept/Dec 14 percent wheat fob Rostock at 312.50 marks.
The Sept/Dec fob barley price is at 245-255.
New crop bread rye was steady at 242.50-247.50 marks fob Aug through first half Sept.
